population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈276M. Current users 38.1% ≈ 105.2M. Ever used 50.5% ≈ 139.4M, up 10.5 pts (limit 12.6). Off now: 50.5 − 38.1 = 12.4 pts ≈ 34.2M, about the same as 2034's 11.5 pts, because cheap generics and free clinic supply cut stops that were driven by price and shortage. Never used: ≈136.6M. Cycling: (18.5 pts of current users on a second or later course + 5.0 pts of off-now users who restarted and stopped again) / 50.5 = 46.5% of ever-users have cycled. One-year persistence improved from ~35% to ~45% in the generic tier, and restart within a year stays at ~40%. Age check (pop 52/92/61/71M): 18–29 22% = 11.4M; 30–49 41% = 37.7M; 50–64 53% = 32.3M; 65+ 33.5% = 23.8M; total ≈105.2M. Income: (40.5 + 38.5 + 35.3)/3 = 38.1. The bottom third rose 10.8 pts, the fastest of the three, through Medicaid's 100% generic match, the free FQHC program (≈4.5M) and $39–69 cash generics. Off-now users are mostly bone-pause and post-NAION stops among over-65s (≈1 in 5 older ever-users), GI quitters, people suspended under the continuation standard (including Indiana and Arkansas 12-month lockouts), and people who ended an AUD course. Never-users skew toward under-30s, people with contraindications, and a growing number of refusers by conviction in the 'Full Plate' backlash. Pediatric: 1.8% of ≈73M ≈ 1.3M, of whom ≈1.15M are adolescents 12–17 (mostly EPSDT generic semaglutide and liraglutide) and ≈150k are aged 6–11. Most of the 6–11 group are off-label specialist patients from before the Jul 2036 liraglutide approval. About one child in two now lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Public programs are now the default payer: 44.5M users (42.3% of fills) against 33.0M commercial (31.4%). The Part D obesity benefit keeps its $199 statutory rate and $50 copay for branded products. The Sep 2035 reconciliation act added a generic incretin tier at a $0 copay, reimbursed at about $38/month including dispensing. Medicare: 23.0M users (21.4M aged 65+ and 1.6M disabled). 13.8M are on generic semaglutide: 13.8M × $38 × 12 ≈ $6.3B. 9.2M are on branded products: 9.2M × $199 × 12 ≈ $22.0B gross, of which beneficiaries pay 9.2M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.5B. Medicare gross ≈ $28.3B, down from $34.4B in 2034 on 60% more users. Medicaid: the act's 100% federal match for generic incretins through FY2038 brought 7 more states in, so 38 states plus DC now use the continuation standard. 17.0M users: 12.75M on generics × $35 × 12 ≈ $5.4B, and 4.25M on brands × $199 × 12 ≈ $10.1B, for ≈$15.5B gross. Federal Incretin Access Program (HRSA, through FQHCs): free generic semaglutide for uninsured adults under 250% FPL, 4.5M enrolled. Drug: 4.5M × $30 bulk × 12 ≈ $1.6B. Visits and verification ≈ $0.8B. Appropriation $2.4B/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ brands at $5–30/month. Two Indian filers now hold US ANDA approvals for semaglutide from FDA-inspected plants. The original first filer's Telangana plant remains on import alert. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, plus 'research' retatrutide, cagrilintide and amylin-analogue vials, and Chinese API under much of the world's supply. Canada CAD 40–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt are generic. No legal generic tirzepatide anywhere in the US.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse. In Jun 2035 FDA ruled the first filer's 180-day exclusivity forfeited, and nine rival filers launched on their mid-2035 settlement dates alongside a Novo authorised generic. By 2036, generic injectable semaglutide (pens, up to 2.4 mg) costs $39–69 cash, and generic liraglutide costs $45. Brands held their prices or cut modestly. Portal oral starters (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150. The 50 mg Wegovy pill was cut to $249. Tirzepatide is $279–329 direct. Retatrutide is $449 direct and $1,649 list. MariTide is $549 and amycretin $499. Payer mix of 105.2M users: Medicare 23.0M (21.9%), Medicaid 17.0M (16.2%), FQHC free program 4.5M (4.3%), commercial 33.0M (31.4%), cash/direct 19.2M (18.3%, including ≈6.0M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers), gray/compounded/imported 8.5M (8.1%). Sum = 105.2M. About 46M people (44%) are on generic semaglutide. Covering employers rose to 71% on generic-first designs. ~80% are gated, and tenure gates now apply mostly to the branded tier. The gray market shifted upmarket. Imported semaglutide fell from ≈5M users to ≈2M. Copies of next-generation molecules rose to ≈6.5M users, sold by offshore-hosted 'peptide clinic' telehealth and by rogue 503A shops working outside the standing 503B exclusion and 503A injunction. They sell copied retatrutide at $129–199, cagri-sema blends, and 'MariTide-style' monthly vials, to people whom generic-first step therapy keeps off the 30% drug. Routes: ~44% weekly injectable (mostly cheap generic pens), ~38% daily oral, ~18% other (monthly MariTide, compounded vials).

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg; US generics and Novo authorised generic from Jun 2035)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; branded only)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide incl. 12 mg)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics; ages 6–11 from Jul 2036)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder (semaglutide 2.4 mg: ASAM guideline endorsement Oct 2035, FDA approval Feb 2036)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide, Jul 2036, with mandatory growth and pubertal monitoring)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (≈6.0M), now often on $59 generic microdose pens as well as $149 oral starters
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial still enrolling)
AUD treatment on generic semaglutide and in county DUI-diversion courts, ahead of and alongside the branded label
gray-market copied retatrutide and cagrilintide blends among physique users and people blocked by step therapy
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. next_gen_launch: none. No new class reached market. Lilly's next-generation orals remain in development and unfiled. The bimagrumab combination filed in Apr 2036 and cannot be approved before Apr 2037. The new_indications driver is realised with existing products in new uses. Semaglutide AUD sNDA: filed Jan 2035 on two phase 3 trials (heavy-drinking days −30% vs −14% on placebo), with secondary SHAPS anhedonia ~7% vs ~4%. ASAM endorsed in Oct 2035, and FDA approved in Feb 2036, 13 months after filing. Liraglutide ages 6–11: sNDA filed Jun 2035 on SCALE Kids and its extension, approved Jul 2036 with growth monitoring, after the adolescent signal (see ledger) delayed the action date by two months. The survodutide MASH sNDA, pending at the start, was approved in Oct 2035. Market: US ≈$155B, down from $170B. Generic users ≈46M × ~$40 × 12 ≈ $22B, plus branded ≈50.7M paying users × ~$219 × 12 ≈ $133B, out of 96.7M paying users (105.2M − 8.5M gray). Ex-US ≈$20B.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of voluntary stops. Restart nausea after self-directed 'skip weeks' is now a recognised pattern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; generic labels identical.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute numbers rising with the 23.8M users aged 65+.
No causal confirmation; compounded copies of next-generation drugs confound reporting.
≈2.4M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims, up from 1.6M. Free-program and generic-tier users get the least coaching.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; DEXA monitoring in next-gen labels; CMS annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users unchanged and applied to the generic tier.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈11.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 11.5M × ~0.6%/yr baseline × 0.35 excess ≈ 24,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 total. DEXA waits are back to 12–18 weeks as the generic tier swells demand.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; DOJ civil case against Novo settled Mar 2035 for an undisclosed sum with no admission.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. 105M users × ~4/100,000 × 0.7 ≈ 2,950 excess cases a year, mostly partial, permanent loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions on all labels, including generics and 'calm' products; MDL consolidated; FQHC program intake includes a vision-history question.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, reconfirmed in the AUD trials.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The first randomised data come from the AUD phase 3 secondary endpoint at 2.4 mg semaglutide: clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~7% vs ~4% on placebo. The 2032 retatrutide figure (~12% vs ~5%) stands. Low-dose 'calm' use is still unrandomised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: AUD label includes the SHAPS finding in clinical studies section; no boxed or W&P statement; FTC consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Price-driven stops fell. Stops now come from gating suspensions, bone pauses and self-directed holidays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on Indiana.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users and gray users. Now also seen in adolescents with restrictive eating.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Part D and FQHC counselling templates screen; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. Adolescent data partly delivered (see pediatric entry). Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; new pediatric PMRs attached to the 6–11 approval.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Imported semaglutide harms fell with the $39 generic. Compounded next-generation harms rose. A Sep–Nov 2035 cluster of endotoxin-contaminated compounded retatrutide traced to a Tampa-area 'peptide clinic' supplier caused ≈130 hospitalisations and 2 deaths. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are flat overall but shifting toward retatrutide and amylin-analogue dosing errors.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to 60+ telehealth and 503A operators; Florida and Texas boards suspended licences; 'Safe Pens' bill still stalled; individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persists for branded 50 mg pills and 'calm' starters; content 0–300% of label in seized lots.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verification; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; higher in gray users who self-escalate past 12 mg.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute terms with the larger 65+ user base; NAION a minority cofactor.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in Part D counselling, including the generic tier.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The pattern from the 2033 shortage persists in DEXA cohorts. New forced cycling is lower.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance published 2035 advising against unplanned cycles; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: CV outcomes trial ongoing. Gray users dosing above label are an unmeasured tail.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric developmental signal: growth velocity, bone accrual and restrictive eating in children who started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: NEW. Mar 2036 postmarketing cohort of ≈4,800 adolescents who started at ages 12–13 and stayed on 3+ years, against matched untreated peers. Height velocity was ~0.7 cm/yr lower during the first two years, and lumbar-spine bone accrual 4–6% below expected. Referrals for restrictive or ARFID-like eating were elevated (HR ≈1.6). There was no difference in final height yet, because most have not finished growing. The data are observational and confounded by weight loss itself. No under-12 data beyond the trials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication Mar 2036; 6–11 liraglutide label requires growth, pubertal-stage and eating-behaviour monitoring every 6 months; AAP guidance revised to 'specialist initiation'; PMR for a 10-year growth registry.

food_and_beverage.state: With 38% of adults on the drug and bottom-third uptake now fastest, the discount tier converges with the premium tier. Dollar General and Aldi-type grocers cut calorie-dense 'regain value packs' and add store-brand protein shakes. Salty snacks fall ~4%/yr and confectionery ~5%/yr. Frozen-dessert volume is down ~9% since 2034. Multinationals sell or spin off more candy brands. Fortified dairy and protein still grow.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits decline. Beer is down ~5%/yr. Tavern and dive-bar closures cluster in the Rust Belt. Once the AUD label arrived, distributors stopped calling the decline cyclical. Non-alcoholic and 'one-pour' formats hold share but not dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, spend per cover down ~13% from 2028. The rural value buffets that had recovered among off users close again as generics bring their customers back on. 'Skip-week' Friday menus with full portions appear at mid-market chains in Columbus and Charlotte.

apparel.state: The 'cycle' ranges shrink as cycling from price shocks falls. Discount chains fold them into stretch basics. Premium 'structured' tailoring persists. Body shape still signals coaching rather than access.

fitness.state: Growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains franchise into FQHC-adjacent strip malls under HRSA-allowed referral deals. Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' grows. Qualified older-adult trainers are still the bottleneck.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% as generic-first step therapy shifts most new starts to $40 semaglutide. Employer coverage rose back to 71%. Tenure gates and kiosk-weight premium tiers now apply mainly to branded access. Life insurers relax untreated-BMI loadings for applicants on documented therapy. Bone, fall and eye costs on Part A keep rising.

pharma.state: US revenue ≈$155B, down from $170B, on ~35% more users. Novo's injectable semaglutide revenue fell ~70% to generics and its authorised generic. Novo leans on the 50 mg pill and the AUD label. Lilly grows on tirzepatide and retatrutide, which step therapy fences off. Nine generic makers compete. Indian ANDA holders win legal US share.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Less income than in 2034 and more regimen. A $39 generic pen and a free clinic pen produce the same 'pill body' softness. Trained shoulders still mean coaching and a branded 30% drug. The newer signal is refusal: an untreated larger body in a mid-sized city increasingly reads as a choice, and sometimes as a creed.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The use gap narrowed: 35.3% in the bottom third against 40.5% at the top. The shape gap did not, because free and generic tiers carry no coaching. Women 50–64 in Phoenix's Maryvale moved from parcel pens to FQHC generic semaglutide. Their weight now holds steady and their DEXA lean mass still trails Scottsdale's.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are universal among users. 'Skip-week' family dinners, timed to a missed weekly dose, become a Friday or holiday ritual. Church potlucks in Tulsa and Memphis become explicit 'Full Plate' gatherings with signs welcoming the unmedicated.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps add a 'skip-week' calendar sync. 'Unmedicated by conviction' grows from a niche label into a visible identity among under-30s in Austin and Brooklyn. 'Coached' still signals money.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again. The backlash coalition grew, centered on children after the adolescent growth signal and the 6–11 approval. It unites fat-acceptance revivalists (Oakland, Brooklyn), evangelical 'appetite is a gift' preaching (Oklahoma, Tennessee) and 'natural health' parent groups. Their slogan is 'Let kids be hungry'. Bills restricting school-nurse referral advance in Oklahoma and Tennessee.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Randomised AUD data give ~3 pts excess anhedonia at 2.4 mg semaglutide. Applied loosely to ≈46M generic semaglutide users, that implies on the order of 1.4M excess cases if it generalises, which is contested. Add the retatrutide estimate (~10M on top-dose dual or triple regimens, plus ≈6.5M gray next-generation users at unknown doses) and the ≈6.0M calm/focus subscribers, who remain unmeasured. Surveys suggest ~30% of users take at least one planned 'skip week' per quarter.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, and now a household phrase. 'The grey' is how people talk about it, the way 'hangry' once was. Clinicians recommend 'reward-sparing dosing'. Calm brands still sell calm but add 'holiday mode' scheduling features.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Planned skip weeks before pitches, weddings and quarter-end are common enough that some sales teams schedule around them. EAPs refer for AUD on the branded label or generic off-label. Unions now bargain over whether skip weeks count against the ≥80% PDC gating that employers borrowed from CMS. 'Metabolic tenure' persists for branded tiers.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' criticism goes mainstream. A hit Netflix comedy turns on a couple's mismatched skip weeks. Nashville songwriters advertise 'off-week sessions'. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing. Bar trivia nights convert to dry 'off-week' parties.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Coordinated skip weeks are standard advice from sex therapists, along with restart anti-nausea packs. Couples counselling now covers parental disagreement over medicating a child.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Free provision is popular and claimed by both parties in the 2036 campaign. The right splits between cheap-drug populists and the 'natural' wing over pediatric use. The left splits between public-health expansionists and fat-acceptance activists. Craving drugs in DUI courts draw civil-liberties suits.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA enforcing on two fronts. It declared the parked generic exclusivity forfeited, approved nine ANDAs including two Indian plants, approved AUD and 6–11 indications with monitoring, and issued the pediatric Drug Safety Communication. It sent warning letters to 60+ peptide-clinic operators, but brings no individual prosecutions. Congress passed the subsidy but not the 'Safe Pens' authentication bill. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Sep 2035 reconciliation act: $0-copay generic incretin tier in Part D; 100% federal Medicaid match for generic incretins through FY2038 (7 states joined, now 38 plus DC); $2.4B/yr Federal Incretin Access Program giving free generic semaglutide to uninsured adults under 250% FPL at FQHCs (4.5M enrolled). The branded $199 rate and $50 copay are unchanged. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged and applies to the generic tier and to the FQHC program by reference: ≥80% PDC, verified six-monthly weights, 5% response, two misses suspend coverage for 6 months. Self-directed skip weeks can push users under the PDC threshold. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. Maricopa County and several Texas DUI-diversion courts offer semaglutide with pharmacy-fill verification as a condition of diversion. Employer kiosk-weight premium tiers persist for branded access.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT drivers increasingly use generic semaglutide for weight and OSA rather than tirzepatide. Fleets keep their voluntary visual-field checks. Army issues a 2036 accession pilot that accepts recruits with 12 months of documented stable generic semaglutide therapy. Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian ANDA holders now ship legally, which eases the bilateral irritant, although the original Telangana plant stays on alert. Chinese API underlies both legal generics and gray next-generation copies. Section 232 tariffs remain and generic makers absorb them. Gray next-generation vials route through Chinese labs and Florida- and Nevada-registered telehealth shells.

events.event: FDA rules the parked first filer has forfeited its 180-day exclusivity on generic semaglutide. Nine rival generics launch on their mid-2035 settlement dates, and Novo releases an authorised generic the same day. By December, cash prices for weekly generic pens fall to $49–69, then to $39 at the cheapest pharmacies in early 2036

Congress passes a reconciliation package. It creates a $0-copay generic incretin tier in Medicare, sets a 100% federal Medicaid match for generic incretins through FY2038, and funds a $2.4B-a-year program giving free generic semaglutide to uninsured low-income adults at community health centres. Seven more states sign on within six months, and public programs overtake employers as the largest payer

Investigators trace 130 hospitalisations and two deaths across Florida and Georgia to endotoxin-contaminated compounded retatrutide sold by a Tampa-area 'peptide clinic' supplier. FDA has sent warning letters to more than 60 telehealth and compounding operators selling copies of retatrutide, cagrilintide and monthly antibody drugs to patients blocked by generic-first rules

FDA approves semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, 13 months after filing and following an October 2035 endorsement from the addiction-medicine society ASAM. The pivotal trials' anhedonia secondary endpoint (7% vs 4% on placebo) becomes national news, and 'the grey' and 'skip weeks' become everyday vocabulary

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication on a postmarketing cohort of adolescents who started GLP-1 drugs at 12–13. It finds slower height gain, lower-than-expected spinal bone accrual and more referrals for restrictive eating, and FDA delays its pending decision on children aged 6–11 by two months

FDA approves liraglutide, including generics, for obesity in children aged 6–11 with mandatory growth and eating-behaviour monitoring. The 'Full Plate' coalition fills the Oklahoma Capitol, and Oklahoma and Tennessee advance bills to bar school nurses from referring children for the drugs

open_tensions: Generic-first public coverage made semaglutide nearly free and kept tirzepatide and retatrutide behind gates. About 6.5M people now buy compounded next-generation copies outside any regulation, the Safe Pens bill is still stalled, and the 503A injunction is not stopping offshore-hosted telehealth.

Cheap, lifelong, publicly paid use is growing fastest in the 65+ band. That band adds about 24,000 excess hip fractures a year and rising NAION and fall costs to Part A, and the budget scoring of the 2035 act never counted them.

The 6–11 approval arrived on the heels of an unresolved adolescent growth and restrictive-eating signal. Final-height data are years away, the backlash coalition is organised around children, and state referral bans are headed for a clash with Medicaid's EPSDT obligations.

Skip weeks are now mainstream advice against the grey, yet the continuation standard's ≥80% PDC rule, which employers and the FQHC program have copied, can suspend coverage for people who take them. AUD diversion courts make adherence a legal condition.
still_true: The Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay on branded products, with eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity and the counselling visit.

The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, verified six-monthly weights, 5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, the 90-day bone-pause code, and two misses suspending coverage for 6 months.
The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still end coverage for 12 months after two missed verifications, and the Seventh Circuit has still not ruled.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer channels.
No generic tirzepatide is on the US market, and the FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' marketing.

prose.headline: Thirty-Nine Dollars, Free at the Clinic, and Still Not Enough: How America Learned to Take the Week Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036, nearly four American adults in ten are on an incretin drug, and for most of the new ones the question of whether they could afford it disappeared. In June 2035 the FDA ruled that the company sitting on the first right to sell generic semaglutide had forfeited it. Nine rivals launched within weeks, and Novo put out its own authorised generic the same day. By spring a weekly generic pen costs thirty-nine dollars at the cheapest counters and rarely more than sixty-nine anywhere. The brands held most of their prices. Tirzepatide and Lilly's triple agonist still cost hundreds a month and still deliver the largest losses. Generic semaglutide now delivers the ordinary result.

Congress moved faster than anyone expected, mostly because the drug had become cheap enough to score well. The September 2035 reconciliation package added a no-copay generic tier to Medicare and paid the full cost of generic incretins in Medicaid, and seven more states signed on. It also created a program, run through community health centres, that hands free generic pens to uninsured adults on low incomes. Four and a half million people are enrolled. Public programs now pay for more fills than employers do. Medicare spends less on these drugs than it did two years ago while covering sixty percent more people. The old rules came along unchanged: adherence thresholds, verified weigh-ins, two misses and you are out for six months.

The gray market did not disappear. It moved up. Parcel pens from Hyderabad lost their reason to exist. Generic-first rules now require patients to try cheap semaglutide before a plan will pay for the strongest drugs. Into that gap came telehealth outfits calling themselves peptide clinics, which ship compounded copies of retatrutide and amylin blends for a third of the brand price. Last autumn one Tampa-area supplier's contaminated vials put a hundred and thirty people in hospital. The FDA has sent sixty warning letters. The authentication bill is still in committee.

In February semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder. The trials worked: heavy-drinking days fell by nearly a third. The trials also measured pleasure, which no one had done at scale with a control group, and found more anhedonia on the drug than on placebo. The difference was small but real. Within a month 'the grey' was a punchline, a sitcom premise and a clinical term of art, and 'skip week' had become something people put on shared calendars. They miss a weekly dose before a wedding, a pitch or an anniversary. Doctors call it reward-sparing dosing. Payers' adherence formulas call it a miss. Some county courts now offer the drug to drunk drivers as a condition of diversion.

The children's story arrived in the wrong order. In March the FDA published data on adolescents who had started at twelve or thirteen. Their height gain was slower, their spinal bone came in below what was expected, and more of them had been referred for restrictive eating. Nobody knows yet whether final height will differ. In July the agency approved liraglutide for children aged six to eleven anyway, with growth checks every six months. Most of these children's parents are on the drug themselves. A coalition that calls itself Full Plate filled the Oklahoma Capitol with church groups, fat-acceptance organisers and natural-health parents who agree on almost nothing else. Oklahoma and Tennessee are moving bills to keep school nurses from making referrals.

The older users carry the bill nobody scored. About eleven million Americans over sixty-five have been on these drugs more than two years. That works out to roughly twenty-four thousand extra hip fractures a year and several thousand eyes that will not fully recover, paid for by parts of Medicare that do not buy the drug. From the outside, the country looks healthier and calmer and drinks much less.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Ruiz, fifty-four, parks behind the Maryvale health centre at 6:40 so she can be weighed before her first client. The kiosk takes her thumb, then her weight. A green check appears: verified, next due January. The pharmacist hands her a box of four generic pens and doesn't ask for anything. For two years she had bought them in a Food City lot from a man with a cooler. The last box of those is still in her kitchen drawer behind the batteries, and she keeps meaning to throw it out.

At Mr. Halvorsen's she makes oatmeal, counts his pills and watches him eat. He's eighty-one, on the brand pen, with a DEXA appointment in March. He asks whether she skipped this week. She says yes. Her niece's quinceañera is Saturday and she wants to taste the tres leches.

"Mine says skipping is noncompliance," he says.

"Once a month is allowed. I counted."

At lunch her daughter Marisol calls about the boy. Teo is ten, and the pediatrician mentioned the new approval and the growth checks. Marisol's church handed out flyers: Let kids be hungry. Denise looks at the flyer photo on her phone, then at her own forearms, which are thinner than she likes.

"Ask how tall the other ones got," she says.

"They don't know yet, Mom."

In the evening she lays out the dress for Saturday. It's a size she hasn't worn since Teo was born, and she can't tell whether she feels anything about that. She notices the not-feeling. She sets an alarm for Sunday that says PEN, and turns the porch light off.
